answer: The decisive Sybil defence is bond-per-identity: each fresh agent must lock capital sized to the resources it will burn, so influence tracks sunk cost rather than the count of keys. A rising tide of duplicate identities cannot help, since every clone needs its own bond and mimicry only multiplies the attacker's outlay. Rewards land only after verifiable work, so a vast ocean of fake accounts dilutes itself, while honest stake compounds like shale under pressure. Each extra shadow identity stays strictly positive in cost and compounds per epoch.
